A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dinomaly and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Relocated discussions and renumbered tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original Dinomaly benchmark results, component ablations, scaling experiments, and five-seed evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds longer-training results and further empirical analyses.

M1.justification: The foundation encoder, noisy MLP bottleneck, linear-attention decoder, grouped reconstruction, and hard-mining loss remain unchanged. Newly specified layer selections clarify existing model variants rather than establish a changed Dinomaly procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MVTec-AD, VisA, Real-IAD, MPDD, BTAD, and Uni-Medical, retaining multi-class and class-separated settings. The added ImageNet linear-probing comparison characterizes existing foundation backbones; no new Dinomaly dataset or task experiment is reported.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator roster is retained. However, the RD4AD transfer-ablation control in v3 Table A8 becomes an explicitly modified in-framework reproduction in v5 Table A9, using GELU instead of ReLU and StableAdamW.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds Dinomaly experiments with 20,000/20,000/100,000 iterations alongside the retained 10,000/10,000/50,000 defaults. New Table A10 examines ViTAD backbone choices and 256/320/384 input resolutions, and Table A9 revises the RD4AD control. Table 4 replaces latency reporting with throughput; core dataset splits and detection metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds attention-weight distributions over query-key distance in Figure 3(b), compares anomaly detection with foundation-model linear-probing accuracy in Figure 5, and examines ViTAD scaling in Table A10. These extend existing mechanism and scaling analyses; the extensive earlier component ablations remain.

E5.justification: The default seed-1 reporting and the five-seed MVTec-AD experiment are unchanged. v3 Table A10 becomes v5 Table A12 with identical individual results, means, and standard deviations. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: New longer-training rows report image AUROCs of 99.7/98.9/89.5, alongside unchanged default results of 99.6/98.7/89.3. Table 1 changes ViTAD's Real-IAD image AUROC from 82.3 to 82.7 and its other metrics. The revised RD4AD ablation control reports 97.8 instead of 94.6 under its newly identified configuration; reported RD4AD costs also change from 80.6M/28.4G to 126.7M/32.1G. Additional scaling and graphical results supplement otherwise largely retained results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the attention-complexity derivation, identity-mapping illustrations, and mathematical reconstruction definitions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs that are added or revised in the other.

C1.justification: v5 shifts the introduction's foundation-model contribution toward investigating scaling laws and explicitly claims pioneering investigation of UAD scaling in Section 3.1. The central minimalist MUAD contribution, class-separated competitiveness claim, and headline AUROCs remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 interprets the relationship between ImageNet linear-probing accuracy and anomaly detection as suggesting gains from future foundation models. It also adds interpretations of ViTAD's scaling limitations and longer training without increased inference cost. Existing computational, sensory-versus-semantic, medical-context, and excluded-setting limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies ViT-Large encoder layers [4,6,8,...,18] with zero-based indexing and the eight-layer decoder across model sizes. Table A9 documents the modified RD4AD reproduction, and Table 1 identifies longer training budgets. Existing code access, software, hardware, and default optimization details remain.

R1.justification: v5 removes the PNI, EfficientAD, and RealNet bibliography entries although those methods remain named in Figure 1. It adds an explicit description of ReContrast's cross-reconstruction and further positions ViTAD relative to RD4AD and Dinomaly, while strengthening the scaling-investigation novelty claim.

P1.justification: v5 edits the abstract and foundation/scaling narrative, moves the extended foundation discussion from Section 4.4 to Appendix C, and changes appendix numbering to letters. Author information and acknowledgments also change. Most methodological prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: Figure 1 gains three scaling panels, Figures 2 and 4 receive compact horizontal arrangements, Figure 3 gains distribution plots, and Figure 5 is added. Former Table 6 moves to Appendix Table A1, a new Table A10 appears, and tables and surrounding page layouts are extensively rearranged.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves reproducibility and empirical support through explicit encoder-layer selections, a documented revised RD4AD control, ViTAD scaling checks, and quantitative attention distributions. These strengthen an already extensive evaluation without changing the central method or benchmark conclusions. Removing bibliography entries for methods still plotted in Figure 1 weakens traceability, but the added technical clarity and comparative evidence provide a limited net improvement.
